title: Banking and the Reserve Bank of India

questions.question: The Reserve Bank of India was established in:
questions.rationale: The RBI began operations in 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934, and was nationalised in 1949.

questions.question: As 'lender of last resort', the RBI:
options: Lends to the general public at concessional rates
Provides funds to banks in distress against collateral
Prints currency only when the government orders
Sets the minimum reserve of gold
questions.rationale: When banks cannot borrow elsewhere, the RBI lends against collateral — the function that prevents solvent banks from collapsing due to temporary runs.

questions.question: With a CRR of 20%, an initial deposit of ₹1,000 can support total credit of:
questions.rationale: The multiplier is 1/CRR = 1/0.20 = 5, so total deposits = 1,000 × 5 = ₹5,000.

questions.question: In credit creation, each successive round of lending becomes smaller because:
options: Banks lend less as they get tired
A fraction (the CRR) must be retained as cash reserve each round
questions.rationale: The CRR must be withheld from every re-deposited amount, so each round shrinks geometrically until the total reaches deposit × 1/CRR.

questions.question: The nationalisation of 14 major Indian banks took place in:
questions.rationale: In 1969, fourteen large private banks were nationalised to direct credit toward agriculture and rural India; six more followed in 1980.

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary function of commercial banks?
options: Acting as banker to the government
questions.rationale: Accepting deposits and lending are the twin primary functions; currency issue, government banking, and the repo rate belong to the RBI.

questions.question: Fixed and recurring deposits are examples of:
questions.rationale: Time deposits are locked for a term and earn higher interest, unlike current or savings accounts which are withdrawable on demand.

questions.question: Which statement about payment banks is correct?
options: They can issue credit cards freely
They accept small deposits and handle payments but cannot lend
They were created by the FRBM Act
questions.rationale: Payment banks (from 2015, per the Nachiket Mor committee vision) take small deposits and offer remittances but must invest in safe instruments — no lending.

questions.question: AU Small Finance Bank and Ujjivan are examples of:
questions.rationale: Small finance banks, licensed from 2015–16, are full-service banks focused on financial inclusion, small loans, and priority-sector lending.

questions.question: When one person's bank loan becomes another person's bank deposit, the process is called:
questions.rationale: Loans returning as fresh deposits let banks lend again minus the CRR — the geometric process through which banks create credit money.
